questions.skill: Verify that rigid motions take angles to angles of the same measure
questions.prompt: Angle ABC has A(4, 0), B(0, 0), and C(3, 3). It is reflected across the y-axis. Find A', B', and C', and explain why angle A'B'C' has the same measure as angle ABC.
questions.prompt_markup:
Angle ABC has A(4, 0), B(0, 0), and C(3, 3). It is reflected across the y-axis.
Find A', B', and C', and explain why angle A'B'C' has the same measure as angle ABC.
questions.correct_answer: A'(-4, 0), B'(0, 0), C'(-3, 3). Ray BC and ray B'C' each run along a diagonal of the grid squares, so each angle is half of a right angle: both measure 45°.
questions.grading_note: Grade both: the three image points, and a check that both angles measure 45°.

questions.skill: Verify that rigid motions take angles to angles of the same measure
questions.prompt: The right triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), and (0, 4) is translated 2 units right and 1 unit up. Find the image vertices, and explain why the angle at the image of (0, 0) is still a right angle.
questions.prompt_markup:
The right triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), and (0, 4) is translated 2 units right and 1 unit up.
Find the image vertices, and explain why the angle at the image of (0, 0) is still a right angle.
questions.correct_answer: (2, 1), (6, 1), and (2, 5). The sides from (2, 1) are horizontal and vertical, so they are perpendicular: the angle is 90°.
questions.grading_note: Grade both: the vertices and the reason.

questions.skill: Prove theorems about parallelograms
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: ABCD is a parallelogram. Prove that angle A and angle B are supplementary. Give a reason for each step.
questions.prompt_markup: ABCD is a parallelogram. Prove that angle A and angle B are supplementary. Give a reason for each step.
questions.required_method: A valid chain of reasons. Other valid orders are accepted. A conclusion without reasons is not full credit. Example: AD ∥ BC (definition of a parallelogram), and AB is a transversal; angles A and B are same-side interior angles, so they are supplementary.

questions.skill: Prove theorems about parallelograms
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 70°. Find the other three angles and give a reason for each.
questions.prompt_markup:
In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 70°.
Find the other three angles and give a reason for each.
questions.correct_answer: Angle B = 110° and angle D = 110° (consecutive angles are supplementary); angle C = 70° (opposite angles are congruent).
questions.grading_note: Grade the angles and the reasons.
